news.title: Why the Labs are Giving away API Credits
news.gist: Flat AI subscriptions lose money on heavy users, so Anthropic and OpenAI added expiring monthly API credits to their higher tiers: the subscription brings the user in and the API grows what they spend.
points: Raising prices risks losing light users and forcing usage pricing feels hostile, so bundled credits are pitched as a third route
The credits reset each billing cycle, don’t raise chat limits, and skip the cheapest plans such as Claude Pro and ChatGPT Plus
OpenAI reportedly halved the value of its $200 ChatGPT plan this fall, then reverted after pushback
Advice: keep the subscription, offer clear pay-as-you-go, size credits plan by plan and make buying more usage a one-click step

news.why: Credits that expire every month are worth only what your team actually uses, so compare a cycle’s real consumption with the same usage on pay-as-you-go before upgrading for them.

news.title: Your customers don’t just want an agent. They want agents.
news.gist: An Irrational Labs experiment found that calling a product one AI agent didn’t lift buying interest, while presenting it as a team of agents did, even though buyers thought that version looked harder to use.
points: Buyers saw the same page for real calendaring, social media and accounting tools, with only headers and feature labels changed
Stated willingness to pay ranked the team framing highest, but none of the gaps were statistically significant
The authors point to the unpacking effect: splitting a whole into named parts makes it seem worth more
They advise showing each job the product does and cutting filler features, not rebranding everything as agents
nums: US software buyers in the experiment
6.3 percentage points
higher likelihood to want the product with the team framing than with the single-agent one
news.why: When a vendor splits a product into several named agents or prices per agent, compare the jobs actually done rather than the number of agents listed.

news.title: Pricing Changes: November 2–8, 2026
news.gist: A mixed developer-tools week: Ably moved to pricing by monthly active users and capped its Free package for the first time, while LogRocket brought back a free plan and Unkey lengthened log retention at no charge.
points: Google is retiring Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash on 1 Dec and will answer their requests with newer models, billed at those models’ rates
Cloudflare AI Search starts usage billing on 1 Dec, a month later than first planned
Together AI removed several serverless models and pointed users to replacements that carry their own rates
Screenshotlayer’s Free plan is now for non-commercial use only, with the same 100 snapshots a month
nums: monthly active users allowed on Ably’s Free package, which had no such cap before

90 days
Unkey Pro log and audit-log retention, up from 7 and 14 days
Cloudflare AI Search overage per million ingestion tokens
news.why: Forced model migrations can change your bill without any action on your part, so check which deprecated models you call before 1 December.

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Report: November 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ month-to-date tally for November, through the 12th, has more developer-tool changes in buyers’ favor than against them, a turn after an October that ran heavily against buyers.
points: On the negative side, Cloudflare for Startups stopped covering Workers AI for new members, and Ably capped its Free package
Bitrise’s Hobby plan now allows unlimited team members and more build minutes, but requires card verification
Val Town is winding down: new sign-ups ended on 10 Nov and all its services end on 10 Jan 2027
Further changes are scheduled before month end, mostly model retirements at Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Cloudflare

news.why: One good fortnight doesn’t undo months of shrinking free tiers; check the scheduled model retirements and startup-credit terms before setting next year’s tooling budget.

patterns.p: GPU-hour and token prices rose at the infrastructure layer, and AI add-ons priced per use followed. Vendors that resell this compute may pass it on next. Lambda Labs, Front and Mentionlytics come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: More changes cost buyers more than saved them money
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that cost buyers more vs less; the other 40 repackage
stats_analysis.p: List-price increases outnumbered cuts two to one, 22 against 11. The rises ran from Front’s per-conversation agent fee to Lightfield, Recharge and MailSlurp lifting mid and entry plans by half, while TaxSlayer, Cedreo and Fill made the deepest cuts. Most of these records come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Nearly half the week involved AI
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that touch AI features or AI pricing
stats_analysis.p: AI changes cover the whole range: token and per-conversation rates went up, image credits bought less, and quota systems gave way to credit wallets at Letta and FlutterFlow. LogicMonitor now includes AI credits with each Hybrid Unit while raising two of its three unit rates.

stats_analysis.t: Limits moved both ways in equal measure
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that loosen vs tighten a limit
stats_analysis.p: Looser limits clustered in developer infrastructure, such as Render’s uncapped sandboxes, Vercel’s longer trace retention and LeadMagic’s doubled exports. Tighter ones clustered in AI generation credits and free plans. Most loosened limits are our own captures, while almost all tightened ones come from PricingSaaS reports, so the balance partly reflects which pages each source watches.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes that switch the unit a price is counted in
stats_analysis.p: TaxDome moved from seats to clients, Seam from devices to credit packs, Ably from usage to monthly active users and ApprovalMax from organization count to document volume. Cohere moved Model Vault to per-GPU rates and FunnelStory moved its agents to outcome-based billing. A unit switch can raise or lower a bill without any headline price change, so rerun your own volumes.

stats_analysis.t: The top of the list is mostly repackaging
stats_analysis.p: Four of the nine repackage: Salesforce moved Momentum out of Core, PagerDuty reshuffled what its flat fees include, Cohere changed Model Vault’s unit and Render dropped a sandbox limit. Three make things cheaper and two raise prices, Together AI’s token rates and Wispr Flow’s smaller educator discount. All nine are our own captures.

news_trends.t: Included credits become the default way to sell AI
news_trends.p: In three straight issues Good Better Best has moved from Notion’s split wallets to credit-design lessons from Gong, Miro and Databricks to the labs bundling API credits into subscriptions. Our records show the same shift: Letta and FlutterFlow swapped fixed AI quotas for credit allowances this week, after ClickUp and Anthropic rebuilt plans around included AI usage the week before.

news_trends.t: Free developer tiers: steady erosion, then a mixed start to November
news_trends.p: AgentDeals logged almost only negative developer-tool moves through October, mostly shrinking free allowances, but its November tally so far tilts positive with LogRocket’s returning free plan and Unkey’s longer retention. Our sample has not turned yet: Hevo, Cargo and Breezy HR cut free access this week, most of it from PricingSaaS reports.

news_trends.t: Model retirements reprice usage by default
news_trends.p: AgentDeals’ digests since mid-October keep listing retired models whose traffic is rerouted or cut off, and the replacement is billed at its own, often higher, rates. This week Together AI removed a Qwen model and named Qwen3.7-Max as its replacement, in the same week it raised Qwen3.7-Max rates by about two thirds.
